history.p: Hartmann wrote his first symphony at a time when only a few Danish composers had had a try in this genre. Shortly after the first performance in Copenhagen, he brought the score with him on his first grand tour in Europe in the spring and summer of 1836, and showed it to Franz Lachner and Louis Spohr. The latter was very enthusiastic and performed it in Kassel. On his second tour in 1839, Hartmann played it for four-hands piano with Mendelssohn; however, the symphony was not performed in Leipzig. 1850-1851 Hartmann reworked the symphony for a performance at Musikforeningen.

event.desc: First performance. At this concert the first movement and the Minuet were played as the first piece in the program, the Andante and Finale as the first piece after the interval.

annot.p: Used for and since the Musikforeningen performance in 1851 - possibly before this. All parts originally had the slow introduction from the 1835 version, which has either been cancelled or pasted over with a sheet with the new slow introduction (this presumably means that the the new slow introduction was only composed at the last moment in 1850) after the parts were copied; the same is true of the first movement, b. 285 to end, which has also been written on a pasted-in sheet. In all parts the final movement has been written out on other music paper with separate pagination and - in several parts - with a new form of composer attribution "af Prof. Ridder Hartmann".
